$comment: Your personal workspace layer. Deep-merged over workspace.json, and it wins. Versioned on an orphan branch pushed only to your fork — never to the shared repo's main. Put anything here whose value differs between developers.

jscad-body-coverage.description: 3D body coverage in jscad-electronics: make getJscadModelForFootprint return a solid for every footprint that should have one, so a part's physical envelope is measurable from its footprint alone (core's measureFootprinterBody -> create-fdm-enclosure clearance checks). Plan: JSCAD-ELECTRONICS-BODY-COVERAGE.md in the workspace root.
jscad-body-coverage.$consumers: Only jscad-electronics carries the patch. core, circuit-json-to-gltf and 3d-viewer consume the bodies and are rebuilt from workspace.json's bundling graph (`./tsc-dev rebuild --from jscad-electronics`), not patched here.

jscad-body-coverage.description: Two remaining same-repo layers; the `audit` layer (the ledger and the renders of every missing body) merged as #330 and is in main. `bodies` fills the gaps and re-renders the same views; `headers` corrects which way up a through-hole pin header is mounted, kept separate because it changes the meaning of `invert` for existing consumers.

bodies.title: Add the missing 3D bodies: 32 of the 35 recorded gaps
bodies.body:
Fills in the gaps recorded by the base PR and re-renders **the same snapshots from the same cameras** — from above and from underneath. Where they showed bare copper they now show the part; that diff is the review. The ledger goes from 35 entries to 3.

Most of this is dispatch, not geometry. `lib/Footprinter3d.tsx` switches on footprinter's `fn` and simply had no arm for these names, while a suitable body sat in `lib/` unreferenced — `SOT-563.tsx` and `BGA.tsx` had never been reachable at all, SOP and SSOP are SOIC with a different lead span, SON/WSON/VSON are DFNs, MLP and QUAD are QFNs.

Parameterised, or built from the footprint, wherever an alias would report a body that is not there:

- `SOT-223` takes its dimensions, so SOT-89 can use it at a third of the volume
- `TO-220` takes `mouldedTab`, because TO-220F encapsulates the tab
- LGA/MLP/QUAD read `w`/`h`, **not** `grid`: for those `grid` is a pad COUNT per side (`lga14` is 4x3 pads), so reading it as millimetres gave a 4 x 3 body for a part that is 2.4 x 2.9. Only `vson` states its outline as a grid.
- `sot` and `sot343` build their leads from the **pads**. Lead count is not a property of a body outline: aliasing `sot` (a six-pin SOT-23) to SOT235 drew five leads under six pads, and `sot343` (SC-70-4) to SOT363 drew six under four. Both are obvious in the underside view, which is why that view exists.

Four new bodies, for parts nothing in the repo resembled: `DPAK` (TO-252 and TO-263 — a moulded body on an exposed tab, placed over the TAB pad because the footprint is asymmetric), `ElectrolyticCapacitor` (radial can; diameter from `d` or from the name, height derived and deliberately generous), `Potentiometer`, and `SmdPushButton` (whose actuator height is a separate prop, because that is what a lid has to clear).

The through-hole bodies are seated and aligned in their own commit: TO-92 and TO-220 both floated above the board and both assumed one lead pattern, so `to92l` and `to92s` landed beside their holes and TO-220 met its holes at the lead TIPS. They now take the plated-hole centres from the footprint. TO-220's rotations are worth a look — `rotation={[0, 55, -55]}`, which both renderers read as RADIANS, so it stood upright only because 271.3° is nearly -90°, and leaned 1.3° off vertical.

`tests/body-coverage/body-envelope.test.ts` is the assertion the pictures cannot make: every body's height above the board, against `NOMINAL_HEIGHT_MM` — the same table the base PR's cameras frame with, so a body cannot pass here while being photographed as though it were another size.

Still open, with reasons in the ledger: `jst` (only the ZH series has a body), `m2host` (footprinter reports no dimensions at all for it), `usbcmidmount` (`USB-C.tsx` draws with `Ellipsoid` and with `rotation` props on primitives; `lib/vanilla` implements neither and ignores the second SILENTLY rather than rejecting it, so reusing it would render the wrong shape).

headers.title: Mount through-hole pin headers on top of the board, not under it
headers.body:
A plain `pinrow` rendered upside down: the plastic body sat at z -3.6 to -1.6, hanging beneath the board with 2mm of pin poking up through the holes — a BOTTOM-mounted header — while `invert` produced the ordinary top-mounted one. The default and the flag were the wrong way round.

Visible in the renders (the holes met the pins at the TOP of the body rather than at its base) and worse in the numbers: the part measured **0.9mm** above the board where a 2.54mm header stands about **8.5mm**. An enclosure sized from that leaves no room for the header at all — the same class of defect as a missing body, and a worse one, because a confidently wrong height reports no `component_bounds_unknown` for anything to fall back on.

`invert` now means what it says: mounted on the underside. `faceup` and the SMD and right-angle variants are unchanged.

Separate from the body work because it changes existing renders — `pinrow6`, `pinrow6-invert`, `pinrow6-faceup`, `pinrow8_rows2`, `pinRow-smd-rightangle` — and changes what `invert` means for anything that passes it. `breakoutheaders` leaves the known-bad list in `body-envelope.test.ts` as a result.
